definitions.meaning: to change or swap one thing for another
the control flicked to turn a light or machine on or off

explanation.surface: Reads as a request to replace a broken power control.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for exchanging things and a noun for an electrical control that opens or closes a circuit.

clue.text: Perhaps wife needs support after blowing top

indicators.note: losing one's top here means the first letter of the word for support is knocked off

parts.note: to support a cause is to espouse it

explanation.surface: A husband says his wife needs backing after she loses her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' suggests an angry outburst; here it removes the first letter, E, from ESPOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife is one example of a married partner, which 'Perhaps' signals as a definition by example.

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tile cracks when something is pressed down on top of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the floor beneath the tile, but it is the past tense of grind and signals the anagram of TILE UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval or pause between parts of a performance is a short break in proceedings.

clue.text: Material in river, short rectangular building block

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a brick is a rectangular block used in building

explanation.surface: Describes some building material in or by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like building stuff to match the brick, but it means fabric; the Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven linen or cotton fabric, a type of cloth or material.

definitions.meaning: the number 11 is written as a 1 next to a 1, a single digit beside another single digit

explanation.surface: Asks whether the members of a team of eleven turn up separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things singly, each in its own turn, is to do them individually, a set phrase for separately.

clue.text: Remarkably modern paper, one trying to impress others

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in a striking, unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A show-off reads a strikingly up-to-date newspaper to impress people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' signals the anagram of MODERN PAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who casually mentions famous acquaintances is seeking to impress listeners with their connections.

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the word for bob

parts.note: to bob up and down is to bounce
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A doorman chases after someone called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is the verb, meaning bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A man employed at a club door to keep out or eject troublemakers is a kind of doorman.

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
mega is slang for excellent or very good

explanation.surface: A romantic praises a fine man from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the written sense.

clue.text: Admission made by unknown female tucking into dish

indicators.note: tucking into means placing these letters inside the dish word

parts.note: an entree is a dish served at a meal
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unidentified woman confesses while eating a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating; here it puts Y and F inside ENTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge paid to get into a venue is the price of admission.

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being very keen-witted when out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters concealed in 'front, I'm extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at six sharp means arriving punctually at exactly the stated hour.

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is let go from the word for unwise

parts.note: imprudent means unwise

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rugby team drops a reckless player from the front row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a rugby position, but it is the definition, meaning cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward child is bold and presumptuous, which is cheeky or disrespectful behaviour.

clue.text: Caught unawares, Spurs dire, out of form

indicators.note: letters out of their proper form are rearranged, which signals the anagram

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur play badly and are caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; 'out of form' signals the anagram of SPURS DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken off guard by something unexpected is to be startled or astonished by it.

indicators.note: erroneously means wrongly, so the letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a drink, mistakenly calling it claret cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret cup is a punch made with red wine; 'erroneously' signals the anagram of AS CLARET CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish theatrical production or display can be called a show, used as a noun.

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is wary of getting near the pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR (charlady) is British for a woman employed to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary and reluctant to take risks is the same as being careful or hesitant.

clue.text: Question university girl about one revolutionary dish

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Che Guevara was the famous Argentine revolutionary
Lorraine is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A student is quizzed over a radical meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word meaning 'concerning', with the girl's name set after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This savoury egg-and-bacon tart from north-eastern France is a classic baked dish.

clue.text: Word for 'improper behaviour' coined abroad by eccentric

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so the letters of the word are spread out in a new order

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or eccentric

explanation.surface: An oddball overseas has invented a term for bad conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' signals the anagram of COINED, giving INDECO; 'coined' looks like the verb for inventing a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum means a lack of propriety or good manners, which is improper conduct.

clue.text: Diagram of interest to Desperate Dan!

definitions.meaning: a circular graph cut into slices showing proportions
Desperate Dan, the strongman of the British comic The Dandy, loved huge cow pies, so a menu of pies would suit him

explanation.surface: A comic-strip glutton studies a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a character in the British comic The Dandy famous for eating enormous cow pies.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle divided into sectors to show shares of a total is a common statistical diagram.

clue.text: Row after character appears in line-up

indicators.note: after puts the word for row behind the word for character

parts.note: one's character is one's identity
a parade is a row, as of shops

explanation.surface: A quarrel follows when a personality turns up in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line of shops, a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A police line-up places a suspect among others for a witness to pick out.

clue.text: Agency worker set off in violent storm

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A temporary employee sets out in terrible weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of SET, giving EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a strong windy storm, often with rain, the classic word for a gale.

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to court danger is to attract it

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in drawing never-ending bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the T off COURT, leaving COUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter, long-lasting ill feeling is a deep-seated grudge or resentment.

indicators.note: leaving means the learner letter goes away from the word for sidetrack

parts.note: to deflect is to turn something aside
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A learner driver is departing after failing to steer aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault or flaw in character or a product is a shortcoming or failing.

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A recruiter gains a new member of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a congregant; it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile or delight someone so they come round to you is to win them over.

clue.text: Anguish in New York following a turn

indicators.note: following places the city letters behind the other pieces

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Distress in Manhattan after a spell of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is a go, as in having your go at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental suffering, the same as anguish.

parts.note: in British slang chronic means very bad or dreadful
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French judgement on an awful recording.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRONIC as 'awful' is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a factual written account of events in order, a kind of record.

clue.text: Notably, a black smock Renoir finally discarded

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: discarded means the chosen letter is thrown out of the word for smock

parts.note: an overall is a loose protective smock

indicators.note: finally means the end letter of the painter's name

explanation.surface: An art writer notes that Renoir finally threw away his black painting smock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded' removes R from OVERALL, leaving OVEALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something matters most of all is to single it out as especially or notably so.

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for dressing is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a sauce is a dressing for food

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone dresses smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without a sounded R, the word for dressing and the answer sound the same; 'well' is the noun, a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring or well is where water rises, so it is the origin of a stream.

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
blue is the colour of the UK Conservative party, whose members are Tories

explanation.surface: Stage plays and an adult movie are paired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue film' suggests something racy; 'blue' is the Conservative colour, and 'film' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy Story is the 1995 Pixar animated feature film about toys that come alive.

indicators.note: on means the pint letters are attached after the seafront word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade along a seafront

explanation.surface: Someone has a swift beer by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like it describes the pint; it means punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt reply is one made without delay, so it is fast or immediate.
